_source: Lincoln Learning's guides give no per-week granularity of their own - assessments are listed per Learning Period only, with no week attached (confirmed against the 38 district LL pacing guides and against Appendix A's own LL cells). Loren confirmed 8/30/26: students do one LL lesson per subject per school day, so week-level pacing is derived from the district's actual 2026-27 school calendar (2026-2027 Visions School Year Calendar FINAL_WIRE, uploaded 8/30/26) rather than transcribed from a guide.
_note: REPLACES the earlier version of this file, which weighted weeks by a rough sense of which had more instructional days without the actual calendar in hand. This version is built from the calendar directly: for each of the 10 LPs, the fixed lesson count already established for the Semester Plan Generator tool (semester-plan-generator_ll_lesson_ranges.json - LP1 1-15, LP2 16-40, LP3 41-63, LP4 64-78, LP5 79-95, LP6 96-113, LP7 114-133, LP8 134-148, LP9 149-169, LP10 170-180, 180 lessons total) is divided by that LP's own real instructional-day count from the calendar (18, 20, 19, 15, 17, 18, 20, 15, 20, 13 - these sum to 175, confirmed against the calendar's own 'Days in LP' column), giving a lessons-per-day rate specific to that LP. Each of the LP's guide weeks (per WEEK_WINDOWS) then gets that rate times its own real day count, rounded to whole lessons by largest-remainder (fractional remainders go to the higher-day-count week first, then the earlier week, so a short week never absorbs a rounding-up lesson it doesn't have the days for). One real calendar week = one guide week for weeks 1-34, with the two fully non-instructional weeks (Thanksgiving recess, Spring recess) skipped entirely rather than numbered - confirmed against every existing WEEK_WINDOWS boundary: LP1-LP9's day sums from the calendar (18, 20, 19, 15, 17, 18, 20, 15, 20) match the calendar's own LP totals exactly under this scheme, with no adjustment needed. Week 19 is the clearest change from the old file: MLK Day (1/18) plus two non-instructional days (1/21-22) leave only 2 real instructional days that week (1/19-20), not the 4 the old file assumed - so LP5's 17 lessons now split 5/5/5/2 across weeks 16-19 instead of 5/4/4/4. Every other week's split is unchanged or within one lesson of the old file, since the earlier weighting had already gotten most of the year close. LP10 is the one place a real decision was needed, not just a calculation: its window (5/17-6/3) spans THREE real calendar weeks (5/17-21: 5 days, 5/24-28: 5 days, 5/31-6/3: 3 days, Memorial Day pulling a day out of the last one) but WEEK_WINDOWS only has two slots for it (35, 36), because every curriculum in this tool runs on a fixed 36-week grid. Per Loren's instruction 8/30/26, the three real weeks were split as evenly as possible across the two slots - 7 real days to week 35, 6 to week 36 - rather than kept as one real week alone and two folded together. That 7/6 split, not a calendar-week boundary, is what produces the 6-lesson/5-lesson week35/week36 split below. This single map is universal - the fixed lesson-range table and the calendar are the same for every grade and subject, so this file uses only those two inputs, nothing grade- or subject-specific. Applies to every LL course: Math (K-8, IM1), ELA (TK, K-8), Science (K-8), HSS (K-8). No checkpoints, module-mastery names, or assessment text included, per Loren's direction - lesson numbers only.
